# Limits

11 declared limits: 8 that hide a problem and 3 that manufacture a finding.

Every limit here carries two artefacts in `limits/`, and the suite asserts the
exact set of findings each one produces. A limit that hides a problem has a
blind artefact that reports nothing at all; a limit that manufactures a finding
has a contrast artefact that is clean. Keeping the two kinds apart is what stops
an honest refusal reading as a limit that has been fixed.

## Limits that hide a problem

### A consent payload held in a variable is not read

The scanner reads literal arguments. A default whose payload is a variable is skipped entirely, so a granted default assembled anywhere other than at the call site is invisible.

Inputs: `js`.

- `limits/variable-indirection.blind.*` reports nothing.
- `limits/variable-indirection.contrast.*` reports `consent-default-granted@error`.

### An aliased or bundled measurement call is not matched

Calls are matched on the name at the call site, so an alias assigned to a variable, or a bundler that renames the function, hides every consent call in the file.

Inputs: `js`.

- `limits/aliased-calls.blind.*` reports nothing.
- `limits/aliased-calls.contrast.*` reports `consent-default-missing@error`.

### A banner built by script has no markup to judge

Every banner finding is made from markup. A banner assembled at runtime leaves an empty container in the document, so none of the twelve banner reasons can be reached however bad the built banner is.

Inputs: `html`.

- `limits/runtime-injected-banner.blind.*` reports nothing.
- `limits/runtime-injected-banner.contrast.*` reports `banner-reject-absent@error`.

### Modality expressed only in a stylesheet is not seen

Whether a banner blocks the page is read from markup signals: a dialog role, an inline position, or an overlay word in the identity. A banner made modal in an external stylesheet is treated as ordinary content, and the modal findings do not run against it.

Inputs: `html`.

- `limits/no-stylesheet-parsing.blind.*` reports nothing.
- `limits/no-stylesheet-parsing.contrast.*` reports `banner-focus-not-moved@error`, `banner-missing-dialog-role@error`.

### A cookie set by a response that was not captured is invisible

The cookie timing findings read the capture they were given. A measurement cookie set by a background request rather than by the document response is simply not in the file, so the pre-consent check passes on a site that does set it.

Inputs: `headers`.

- `limits/single-captured-exchange.blind.*` reports nothing.
- `limits/single-captured-exchange.contrast.*` reports `cookie-analytics-set-before-consent@error`.

### A tracker outside the documented host list is not recognised

Tracker recognition is a closed list in src/vocabulary.mjs. A measurement endpoint on a first party host, a self hosted collector, or a vendor not on the list is read as an ordinary script.

Inputs: `html`.

- `limits/closed-tracker-host-list.blind.*` reports nothing.
- `limits/closed-tracker-host-list.contrast.*` reports `script-tag-unconditional-third-party@error`.

### A request target assembled at runtime is not resolved

The scanner reads literals and refuses to guess at anything else, so a target that is decoded, concatenated or read from configuration carries no host it can match against the tracker list.

Inputs: `js`.

- `limits/encoded-request-target.blind.*` reports nothing.
- `limits/encoded-request-target.contrast.*` reports `beacon-before-consent@error`.

### An unescaped angle bracket inside an attribute truncates the tag

The element reader finds the end of a start tag by looking for the next angle bracket, so a raw one inside an attribute value ends the tag early. The attribute it was in is lost, the rest of the tag becomes text, and a control whose label carried the bracket is no longer recognised by its words. Writing the bracket as an entity restores the finding, which is what the two artefacts here show.

Inputs: `html`.

- `limits/unescaped-angle-bracket.blind.*` reports nothing.
- `limits/unescaped-angle-bracket.contrast.*` reports `banner-reject-absent@error`.

## Limits that manufacture a finding

### Position in the file is read as order of execution

Whether something happens before the decision is judged by where it sits relative to the consent gate in the source. A function declared above the gate and called from the consent handler is reported, although it runs afterwards. Moving the declaration below the gate clears the report without changing a line of behaviour, which is the clearest possible demonstration that the finding is about position.

Inputs: `js`.

- `limits/source-order-not-execution-order.blind.*` reports `beacon-before-consent@error`.
- `limits/source-order-not-execution-order.contrast.*` reports nothing.

### A consent check inside a custom template is not visible in the export

A container export carries the body of a custom HTML tag but not the behaviour of a custom template, and a tag that gates correctly inside its own code is reported as ungated. The report is still the right default: a gate the container cannot see is a gate nobody reviewing the container can audit.

Inputs: `container`.

- `limits/custom-template-consent.blind.*` reports `tag-custom-html-unchecked@error`.
- `limits/custom-template-consent.contrast.*` reports nothing.

### A capture carries no declared basis for a cookie

The header format has nowhere to say that a cookie is strictly necessary, so a short lived throttling cookie whose name begins like a measurement cookie is reported in the pre-consent phase. The name is the only evidence in the file, and reporting on it is better than assuming.

Inputs: `headers`.

- `limits/capture-has-no-basis-field.blind.*` reports `cookie-analytics-set-before-consent@error`.
- `limits/capture-has-no-basis-field.contrast.*` reports nothing.

## How the corpus is held to this

There are 21 pattern pairs and 19 fixtures beside these 11 limits.
Each one declares the exact set of findings it produces, compared in both
directions, so a false positive shows up as a corrected artefact that still
reports something rather than passing unnoticed.
